'''Vigen Malumian ('''Armenian: Վիգեն Հայկի Մալումյան)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.panorama.am/am/news/2022/03/11/%D5%8E%D5%AB%D5%A3%D5%A5%D5%B6-%D5%84%D5%A1%D5%AC%D5%B8%D6%82%D5%B4%D5%B5%D5%A1%D5%B6/2652441 | title=Նշվում է աստղագետ Վիգեն Մալումյանի 90-ամյակը }}</ref> (Russian: Виген Гайкович Малумян)<ref>{{cite web | url=https://prochtenie.org/fullcatalog/7517 | title=Используемая литература: где скачать и купить, авторы: Шо, Федорова, Reichenbach, Вологодский, Грибашев, Головань, Научно-исследовательский, Федоров, Российская, Слободин, Grimm, Баранов, Мартынов, Молчанов, Horatius, Якоби, Pihlemann, Цепелевич, Брюквина, Солженицын, рефераты и курсовые }}</ref> (11 March 1932 – 2 February 2013) was an Armenian [[Astrophysics|astrophysicist]] who specialised in [[Radio galaxy|radio galaxies]] and the radio characteristics of [[Spiral galaxy|spiral galaxies]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=ՄԱԼՈՒՄՅԱՆ ՎԻԳԵՆ ՀԱՅԿԻ ԾՆՆԴՅԱՆ 90 ԱՄՅԱԿ |url=https://www.bao.am/seminars/pdf/2022/07032022_1.pdf |website=www.bao.am}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=ARMENIAN ASTRONOMICAL SOCIETY ArAS Newsletter March 2022 |url=https://www.aras.am/ArasNews/arasnews151.pdf |website=www.aras.am}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aras.am/Members/MalumianVigen.htm|title=Malumian Vigen|website=www.aras.am}}</ref> He was a prominent [[scientist]] at the [[Byurakan Observatory]] in [[Armenia]] (BAO), a professor at the Faculty of Physics at [[Yerevan State University]], and a member of the BAO Scientific Board.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />  Additionally, he was involved in the scientific council responsible for awarding degrees at the Observatory. Malumian was also a member of several international scientific organizations, including the [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU), the [[European Astronomical Society|European Astronomical Society (EAS)]], and the Armenian Astronomical Society (ArAS).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

== Life and career ==
Malumian graduated in 1954 from the Faculty of Physics and Mathematics at Yerevan State University in Armenia.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> He began working at the Byurakan Astrophysical Observatory shortly thereafter.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />  From 1955 to 1959, he studied in graduate school and defended his candidate dissertation at Yerevan State University in 1963.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />  His dissertation, titled ''Results of Observations of Certain Galactic Radio Sources at 33 cm Using High-Resolution Radio Telescopes'', was supervised by the renowned radio astronomer Semyon Emanuelovich Khaykin.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />

In 1991, Malumian was awarded a Doctorate of Physical and Mathematical Sciences at the Byurakan Astrophysical Observatory, following his research on ''Radio Emission from Moderately Active and Weak Radio Galaxies''.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />  His work focused on isolated and [[Interacting galaxy|interacting galaxies]], [[galaxy group]]s, [[Radio galaxy|radio galaxies]], [[quasar]]s, and other radio sources in multiple wavelength domains. Malumian authored more than 90 scientific papers, many of which were widely cited in international [[scientific literature]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />  He presented his research at numerous international scientific conferences.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />
[[File:Vigen Malumian at a summit.jpg|alt=Vigen Malumian at a summit|thumb|Vigen Malumian at a summit]]
Malumian was also active within the IAU, where he participated in IAU Symposium 194. He held memberships in various IAU divisions, including Division B Facilities, Technologies, and [[Data science|Data Science]], Commission 40 [[Radio astronomy|Radio Astronomy]] (until 2013), and Division X Radio Astronomy (until 2012).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/8683/|title=International Astronomical Union &#124; IAU|website=www.iau.org}}</ref>

Malumian died in Yerevan on 2 February 2013, at the age of 80.<ref>{{cite web |title=ArAS Newsletter, 31 March 2017 |url=https://www.aras.am/ArasNews/arasnews103.pdf |website=ArAS |access-date=15 October 2025}}</ref>
